summary: Enchantment::doPostHurt and Enchantment::doPostAttack are called twice for players
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Launch Minecraft Java Edition 1.20.1.
2. Create a new Creative world with default settings.
3. Obtain a sword and apply Bane of Arthropods to it using `/enchant @p minecraft:bane_of_arthropods 1`.
4. Attack a target for which Bane of Arthropods applies.
5. Observe that the target receives the Slowness effect twice.
6. Obtain armor and apply Thorns to it using `/enchant @p minecraft:thorns 1`.
7. Have another player attack the player wearing the Thorns-enchanted armor.
8. Observe that Thorns damages the attacker twice and reduces the armor's durability twice.
Environment: Minecraft Java Edition Versions: 1.18.1, 22w03a, 22w05a, 1.18.2, 1.19.2, 1.19.4 Pre-release 3, 1.20.1, 1.20.2 (includes snapshots)
Observed Behavior: In Minecraft Java Edition 1.18.1 through 1.20.1, EnchantmentHelper.doPostHurtEffects and EnchantmentHelper.doPostDamageEffects can process the same enchantment twice when a player is involved. Each method first iterates over the entity’s complete inventory through getAllSlots(), which includes the main-hand item, and then performs another iteration over the main-hand item when the relevant entity is a player. As a result, Enchantment.doPostHurt or Enchantment.doPostAttack may be invoked twice for the same enchanted item during a single interaction. This causes enchantment effects to be applied twice, such as Bane of Arthropods applying Slowness twice and Thorns damaging the attacker twice while also reducing the durability of the Thorns item twice.
Expected Behavior: Enchantment post-hurt and post-attack callbacks should be invoked only once for a player during each relevant combat event. Bane of Arthropods should apply Slowness once, while Thorns should damage the attacker once and reduce the enchanted item’s durability only once. Other enchantment effects should likewise not be duplicated because the player’s inventory and equipped item are processed redundantly.
